svg.title: Manovia v2.0 architecture poster
svg.desc: Three columns: the device with the app shell, the compiled safety bundle and the on-device Private Mode path; the FastAPI server with the deterministic crisis gate, the ML backstop that may only raise caution, retrieval, the LLM chain and the output guard; and the ML platform with the catalogue, DVC data, training, MLflow, release gates, cards and the serving seam. A footer states the guarantees, the measured numbers and what is research only.
svg.text: Manovia v2.0 — architecture
Privacy-first, safety-first self-help companion. Portfolio demo — not a clinical service. Not therapy, not a diagnosis, not a crisis service.
Device — the browser (and nothing else)
React + Vite + TypeScript PWA
Lazy routes; initial JS 133.1 KB gzip of a 135 KB budget.
Compiled safety bundle (statically imported)
normalise + crisis rules + escalation + output guard,
built from backend/app/content/** and gated by --check.
Parity with Python: 500/500 phrases, 0 mismatches.
Private Mode (lazy chunk, 30.9 KB gzip)
Same rules engine in the browser; reply from a local
model if one is pinned, otherwise from templates.
Messages encrypted with AES-GCM into IndexedDB;
key derived from a passphrase the server never sees.
No request is made for the whole conversation.
Service worker + local outbox
Precache 744.5 KB of an 800 KB budget. Offline:
"Need help now" and breathing exercises; pending
check-ins replay with client_id when back online.
Microphone, WebXR, camera-free calm space
Voice opens on a button, not a listener. The calm
space is 36 triangles, 5.8 KB gzip, 2D without WebXR.
Sensory profile + "I'm overwhelmed"
Motion, sound, density, contrast and text size, stored
in this browser only; the app may offer, never switch.
prefers-reduced-motion respected everywhere.
Server — FastAPI (the only write path)
Auth, consent gate, owner-only lookup, rate limit
Guest → consent → session; deletion is re-authenticated.
1. Crisis gate — deterministic rules, first
High or imminent risk: pre-written card + helplines,
and no language model is called at all.
2. ML backstop — may only raise caution
Calibrated TF-IDF + rules ensemble; it can never lower
a level, never writes the card, never sees identifiers.
3. Redaction + emotion → retrieval
Curated knowledge base, hybrid BM25 + dense + rerank,
with a calibrated "no good answer" floor.
4. LLM chain (provider-abstracted)
anthropic → ollama → canned supportive reply; a Fake
provider keeps the whole suite offline and deterministic.
5. Output guard — every reply, before it is stored
No diagnosis, no medication dose, no promise, no
prompt leak; a failed reply is replaced, not shown.
Encrypted storage
AES-GCM field + envelope
keys; raw text never logged.
Operator controls
12 kill switches, flip with
no restart; privacy-only drift.
Consented, time-limited clinician share
Ciphertext + key in the URL fragment; the server holds
no key, only a token hash. PDF and HL7 FHIR R4.
ML platform — ml/ (research; deploys nothing)
Dataset catalogue + licences
17 datasets, 10 marked restricted; "DO NOT USE" is a verdict.
DVC-versioned splits (no bytes in Git)
Byte-stable manifests; dvc.lock is a reproducibility gate.
Training — configs as data
Linear, LoRA (XLM-R) and sequence models; seeds pinned;
unknown config keys are errors, not warnings.
MLflow file store — every run
commit (+dirty flag), dataset hashes, resolved config,
seed, library versions, metrics and artefacts.
Release gates (CI fails, not warns)
Reproducibility vs committed baselines · size and INT8
ratios · fairness across 11 identity dimensions (largest
gap 0.026 of a 0.10 ceiling) · DP budget · licence verdicts.
Reports and cards (committed)
Every number in the README has a report and a run id;
a model without a card is an anecdote, not a claim.
Serving seam — the only door to the product
SAFETY_ML · EMOTION_ANALYZER · RETRIEVER · PRIVATE_LLM_MODEL_ID
Research only — not served
Federated + DP, contextual bandit, neural forecast.
/api/v1
gated release
no network
Guarantees, in the order they are enforced: rules decide risk before any model call · a model may only raise caution · every reply passes the output guard.
Raw text is never logged · identifiers never enter a prompt · the share key never reaches the server · no clinical claim is made or implied.
Measured 2026-10-20 (v2.0.0): crisis recall 1.000 / precision 0.543 (dev split) · emotion macro-F1 0.804 · retrieval MRR 0.658 · response 60/60 · agent 40/40.
5,516 backend tests at 94.26% statements · 2,917 frontend tests · initial JS 133.1 KB gzip of 135 KB · precache 744.5 KB of 800 KB · fairness gap 0.026 of 0.10.
Research only, labelled as such everywhere: the mood sequence models (they lost to a 7-day moving average), federated learning with DP, the contextual bandit.
Solid arrows: a request or a gated release. Dashed violet: the on-device path and the research-to-serving seam. Argument: docs/technical-report.md.
Before real users rely on this: clinical review · native-speaker review (Hindi, Bengali) · ethics and legal review · security review by someone else · user research.
